name: VA-11
label: Safe D

key_factors: Strong Democratic district with an 18-point partisan lean
Incumbent Walkinshaw has a massive financial advantage ($2.8M raised vs ~$11K)
No public polling, so forecast rests on fundamentals
model.rationale: The district's 18-point Democratic lean, Walkinshaw's incumbency and overwhelming fundraising edge, and markets pricing a Democratic win near certainty all point to a Safe D race. With no polls or expert ratings available, the fundamentals-based margin of roughly 24 points stands with wide uncertainty.
model.watch: Any late polling showing a much tighter race or a major outside-spending surge for Purves would be the first sign of movement.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Northern Virginia's 11th District is solidly Democratic territory, with an 18-point partisan lean, and first-term incumbent James Walkinshaw is running for a full term after winning the seat. He has raised about $2.8 million and holds nearly $1 million on hand, with substantial outside support, while Republican Arthur Purves has raised only about $11,000 with $200 remaining. A Green candidate also appears on the ballot but lacks visible resources.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings are available for this race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, the money gap, and prediction markets, which price a Democratic win at 97 percent. Everything points to a comfortable Democratic hold, though the absence of polling leaves some room for error.
